subject: Post-call: model fit notes + requested eval artifacts and pin options
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Howard <alex@finlytics.io>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@finlytics.io>
Date: 2026-06-30T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap + next steps (eval materials & model candidates)

Hi Alex / Samir,

Thanks again for the call this morning — appreciate the clarity on the ingestion pipeline and the 95th percentile latency target (<= 450ms). Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

- Goal: Replace current on-prem answer-generation service with a Redwood-hosted inference endpoint that meets your latency target while keeping false-positive rate under 3% on the labeled QA test set.
- Key constraints you called out: redaction of PII before sending, retention window of logs <= 30 days, and SOC2 evidence for data flows.

Immediate next steps I’ll do:
- Share an eval pack (small benchmark, prompts, and a short instruction set) so you can repro local QA. Attachment: finlytics-eval-pack-v1.zip.
- Recommend two model candidates for initial fit testing: rdm-large-qa-v2 (strong on factuality) and rdm-7b-quant-surge (lower latency, slightly lower factuality).
- Provide a short prompt-set and example scoring rubric so your ML engineer can run regression checks. Attachment: prompt-set-finlytics-v3.jsonl.

Could you confirm who on your side will run the eval (name/email) and whether the team prefers us to pin a stable model version for trial or to test against the live catalog first?

I’ll loop in Ben (solutions) and Rishi (account lead) for any technical/pin work.

Cheers,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[jordan_blake@redwood.ai] | +1 (415) 555-0138

--
Attachments referenced: finlytics-eval-pack-v1.zip (contains prompts, eval harness README, small labeled set).

From: Alex Howard <alex@finlytics.io>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@finlytics.io>
Date: 2026-06-30T15:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps (eval materials & model candidates)

Thanks Jordan — this looks good and thanks for the quick follow-up. A couple of clarifying items from the QA team after skimming the eval pack: 

1) Concern: We recently saw a spike in hallucination-like answers after a provider-side model revision in mid-June. Before we proceed with any open-catalog testing we need either (a) a pinned model version that’s known to match the behaviors in your eval, or (b) a diff report describing what changed (tokenizer, post-processing, sampling defaults).

2) Can you confirm whether rdm-large-qa-v2 has been run on long-context examples (>= 2k tokens)? Our documents often span multi-page legal contracts.

3) The procurement team (cc Samir) will need a simple statement of how long logs are retained in the hosted trial and whether we can configure 30-day retention.

If you can provide the diff summary and an explicit pin option we can fast-track an internal run and share results by EOD Friday.

—Alex
Alex Howard
Senior ML Engineer | Finlytics
alex@finlytics.io

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Howard <alex@finlytics.io>, Samir Patel <samir@finlytics.io>
Date: 2026-06-30T17:09:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Re: Post-call recap + next steps (eval materials & model candidates)

Ben / Rishi — looping you in after Alex’s note. Key asks from Finlytics:

- Provide a concise model-diff summary for the mid-June provider update (what changed, impact on sampling/tokenization/postproc).
- Confirm whether rdm-large-qa-v2 has been validated on long-contexts (>=2k tokens) and share any stats.
- Offer a pin or rollback option for the trial so Finlytics can run evaluations on a stable model snapshot.

Proposed short plan:
1) Ben: produce a 1–2 page diff summary (pdf) and attach the test run logs for the two model candidates.
2) Rishi: propose pricing for a one-month pinned trial + a support window for regression triage (can be small, e.g., 4 hours).
3) Jordan: share Drive link with benchmark report and HubSpot record (done).

Alex / Samir — if you prefer, Ben can also produce a short side-by-side example from the June run showing the problematic sample.

Thanks,
Jordan

--
Forwarded attachments suggested: model-diff-summary-20260630.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Howard <alex@finlytics.io>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@finlytics.io>
Date: 2026-07-01T09:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps (eval materials & model candidates)

Alex / team — thanks for flagging this. Attaching a short summary and immediate mitigation options. Attachment: model-diff-summary-20260630.pdf

High-level summary (TL;DR):
- Mid-June change: default sampling temperature reduced from 0.9 to 0.7 in the live catalog for a subset of rdm-large variants; minor tokenizer normalization patch (handles unusual unicode ligatures). No architectural weight changes.
- Observed impact: on our internal QA, some previously longer, cautious outputs became shorter and occasionally omitted clarifying qualifiers — that can look like a hallucination when the model drops caveats.
- Long-context behavior: rdm-large-qa-v2 has been validated up to 4k tokens using chunking + cross-window KV cache; end-to-end latency stays within ~30% of baseline for large batches but single-request P95 may exceed Finlytics’ 450ms target for very large inputs. rdm-7b-quant-surge stays well under 450ms for 2k tokens but has slightly higher factuality variance.

Mitigation options we can offer for the trial:
A) Pin a snapshot of rdm-large-qa-v2 as-of 2026-06-01 (no sampling change) — we’ll reserve the slot for the trial and keep it stable. Estimated cost: $X/month (we’ll put concrete numbers after Rishi weighs in).
B) Apply a sampling/temperature override in the hosted endpoint to emulate the pre-June behavior (server-side parameter change, reversible).
C) Provide a side-by-side diff report and 10 failing examples (redacted) from the June run so your team can reproduce locally.

Attachments included in this thread: model-diff-summary-20260630.pdf, sample-failures-20260630.csv (redacted), finlytics-eval-pack-v1.zip

Next steps I suggest:
- If you want the fastest path to a reproducible eval, accept option A (pin snapshot). We can spin up a pinned endpoint by Wednesday and grant a 30-day log retention configuration for the trial.
- If you want to balance cost, choose option B and we’ll provide the parameter set to run against the live catalog — easier & cheaper but slightly less deterministically stable.

Jordan / Rishi — I’ll follow up with a short doc on how to request a pin (API call + Console checkbox).

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

--
Attachments: model-diff-summary-20260630.pdf (pdf), sample-failures-20260630.csv (csv), finlytics-eval-pack-v1.zip (zip)
